000830: // The GNU attributes a struct or union definition carries on the definition
000831: // itself, either before the tag (`struct __attribute__((packed)) P { ... }`)
000832: // or after the closing brace (`struct P { ... } __attribute__((packed));`).
000833: // They live in a side table rather than in CType because the population is a
000834: // handful of aggregates in a translation unit while the type table is tens of
000835: // thousands of entries: a flag word per type would grow every one of them.
000836: // Both layout engines -- the sizeof folding in c_parse.c and the IR layout in
000837: // c_gen.c -- read this table, and they must agree or a folded sizeof
000838: // contradicts the object it sizes.
000839: typedef struct CAggregateAttributes CAggregateAttributes;
000840: struct CAggregateAttributes
000841: {
000842:     u32 type_index;
000843:     // Range into CParseResult.alignments, as CMember/CDeclaration name theirs.
000844:     u32 alignment_start;
000845:     u32 alignment_count;
000846:     bool is_packed;
000847:     u8 reserved[3];
000848: };
000849: 
000850: // The alignment a declarator wrote on the *type* it declares rather than on an
000851: // object it declares: `typedef int cache_line __attribute__((aligned(64)))`.
000852: // GNU `aligned` there sets the alignment of the type, so unlike every other
000853: // alignment record in this file it *replaces* the natural alignment instead of
000854: // raising it, and it is the one place the attribute lowers one without
000855: // `packed` -- `typedef int pair __attribute__((aligned(2)))` is two-byte
000856: // aligned in both GCC and Clang. The record keys on the alias copy the
000857: // declarator made, never on the type it aliases, so `int` keeps its own
000858: // alignment -- and on every qualified copy of that alias, because a qualifier
000859: // cannot take an alignment away and the qualified copy points past the alias
000860: // at the type it strips to (#714). It lives in a side table for the reason
000861: // CParseResult.noreturn_function_types does: the population is a handful of
000862: // typedefs per translation unit against a type table of tens of thousands of
000863: // entries, so a field on CType would cost every one of them.
000864: typedef struct CTypeAlignment CTypeAlignment;
000865: struct CTypeAlignment
000866: {
000867:     u32 type_index;
000868:     // Range into CParseResult.alignments, as CMember/CDeclaration name theirs.
000869:     u32 alignment_start;
000870:     u32 alignment_count;
000871: };

005801: // The per-64-token class projection of one lexed run, built once when the run
005802: // becomes a source frame and read by every per-line scan of the driver below.
005803: //
005804: // Every one of those scans asks the same closed set of questions of a token —
005805: // does the line end here, is this a parenthesis, can this name a macro — and
005806: // the one-byte shape sidecar answers all of them without touching a 12-byte
005807: // row, so 64 tokens are one masked load and four compares. What that buys is
005808: // not the compare but the advance: a line end becomes a trailing-zero count
005809: // instead of a nine-step row loop with a mispredicted exit, and the
005810: // parenthesis and macro-name scans visit only the lanes that can answer
005811: // (12% and 20% of the stream on this workload) instead of every token of
005812: // every line. C_TOKEN_INVALID is 0, so the masked tail lanes of the last
005813: // window match no class and need no separate trim.
005814: #define C_PP_CLASS_MASK_WINDOW 64

005789: // The row scan the mask projection below replaces, kept as the definition of
005790: // a line's end for a run that carries no shape sidecar and as the reference
005791: // c_test_pp_class_masks_agree holds the mask path to.
005792: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u64 c_preprocess_line_end(CLexResult lex, u64 token_index)
005793: {
005794:     while (token_index < lex.token_count && lex.tokens[token_index].kind != C_TOKEN_NEWLINE && lex.tokens[token_index].kind != C_TOKEN_END_OF_FILE)
005795:     {
005796:         token_index += 1;
005797:     }
005798:     return token_index;
005799: }
005800: 
005801: // The per-64-token class projection of one lexed run, built once when the run
005802: // becomes a source frame and read by every per-line scan of the driver below.
005803: //
005804: // Every one of those scans asks the same closed set of questions of a token —
005805: // does the line end here, is this a parenthesis, can this name a macro — and
005806: // the one-byte shape sidecar answers all of them without touching a 12-byte
005807: // row, so 64 tokens are one masked load and four compares. What that buys is
005808: // not the compare but the advance: a line end becomes a trailing-zero count
005809: // instead of a nine-step row loop with a mispredicted exit, and the
005810: // parenthesis and macro-name scans visit only the lanes that can answer
005811: // (12% and 20% of the stream on this workload) instead of every token of
005812: // every line. C_TOKEN_INVALID is 0, so the masked tail lanes of the last
005813: // window match no class and need no separate trim.

002462: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL CTypeId c_parse_direct_expression_base(CPreprocessResult preprocess, CParseResult* result, CScopeId scope,
002463:                                                          u32 base_start, u32 base_end)
002464: {
002465:     CTypeId type = C_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
002466:     bool call_base = base_end > base_start + 2 && preprocess.tokens[base_start].kind == C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER &&
002467:                      c_token_is_punctuator(&preprocess.tokens[base_start + 1], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS) &&
002468:                      c_token_is_punctuator(&preprocess.tokens[base_end - 1], C_PUNCTUATOR_RIGHT_PARENTHESIS);
002469:     if ((base_end == base_start + 1 || call_base) && preprocess.tokens[base_start].kind == C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER)
002470:     {
002471:         CEntityId entity_id = C_ENTITY_ID_INVALID;
002472:         u32 base_use_index = c_parse_identifier_use_index(result, base_start);
002473:         if (base_use_index != C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
002474:         {
002475:             entity_id = result->identifier_uses[base_use_index].entity;
002476:         }
002477:         CScopeId lookup_scope = scope;
002478:         if (lookup_scope.value == C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && result->scope_count)
002479:         {
002480:             lookup_scope = (CScopeId){
002481:                 .value = 0,
002482:             };
002483:         }
002484:         if (entity_id.value == C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && lookup_scope.value != C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
002485:         {
002486:             entity_id = c_parse_lookup_entity_token(result, preprocess.spelling_base, lookup_scope, &preprocess.tokens[base_start]);
002487:         }
002488:         type = entity_id.value < result->entity_count && result->entities[entity_id.value].kind != C_ENTITY_TYPEDEF &&
002489:                        result->entities[entity_id.value].kind != C_ENTITY_ENUMERATOR
002490:                    ? result->entities[entity_id.value].type
002491:                    : C_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
002492:         // A call base -- `_PyBaseExceptionObject_cast(self)->context` is what
002493:         // CPython's Py_XSETREF callers hand _Py_TYPEOF -- contributes its
002494:         // return type, through a function pointer's pointee when the name
002495:         // binds to one.
002496:         if (call_base && type.value < result->type_count)
002497:         {
002498:             CType* base_type = &result->types[type.value];
002499:             if (base_type->kind == C_TYPE_POINTER && base_type->element_type.value < result->type_count)
002500:             {
002501:                 base_type = &result->types[base_type->element_type.value];
002502:             }
002503:             type = base_type->kind == C_TYPE_FUNCTION ? base_type->return_type : C_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
002504:         }
002505:         else if (call_base && entity_id.value == C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
002506:         {
002507:             CBfloat16Builtin const* builtin = c_parse_bfloat16_builtin(c_token_spelling(preprocess.spelling_base, preprocess.tokens[base_start]));
002508:             if (builtin)
002509:             {
002510:                 c_parse_position_index_append(result->arena, &result->bfloat16_builtin_calls, &result->bfloat16_builtin_call_count,
002511:                                                &result->bfloat16_builtin_call_capacity, base_start);
002512:                 type = c_parse_bfloat16_builtin_result(result, builtin);
002513:             }
002514:         }
002515:     }
002516:     else if (base_start < base_end && c_token_is_punctuator(&preprocess.tokens[base_start], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS))
002517:     {
002518:         // A cast base: `((propertyobject *) new)->prop_name` is what
002519:         // Py_SETREF writes through _Py_TYPEOF, so `__typeof__` over it must
002520:         // resolve or the declaration it types declares nothing.  The cast's
002521:         // own type is the whole answer -- the operand after it only carries
002522:         // the value -- and the machineless resolvers exist exactly for walks
002523:         // like this one that may run inside a machine step.
002524:         u32 cast_close = c_parse_matching_delimiter_indexed(result, preprocess, base_start);
002525:         if (cast_close < base_end && cast_close + 1 < base_end)
002526:         {

002530:             {
002531:                 cast_type = c_parse_pointer_chain(result, preprocess, cast_type, &type_index, cast_close);
002532:                 if (type_index == cast_close)
002533:                 {
002534:                     type = cast_type;
002535:                 }
002536:             }
002537:         }
002538:     }
002539:     return type;
002540: }

004422: // C11 6.3.2.3p3 gives a null pointer constant two spellings: an integer
004423: // constant expression with the value 0, or such an expression cast to
004424: // `void *`.  The second is the only one that survives as a conditional
004425: // operand, and it is what musl's <tgmath.h> selects a type with --
004426: // `0 ? (t *)0 : (void *)!(c)` names `t` exactly when the `void *` arm is one.
004427: //
004428: // The type gate is not a shortcut, it is the whole correctness of the answer:
004429: // the constant walk below strips every cast before evaluating, so
004430: // `(double *)0` folds to zero just as `(void *)0` does, and without the gate
004431: // any zero-valued pointer cast would claim to be a null pointer constant.
004432: // The walk is entered machineless -- the caller is already inside a type-parse
004433: // frame -- so an operand whose value needs the machine (a `sizeof` over a type
004434: // only a frame can resolve) simply answers no, which is the conservative half.

004441:     {

004627: // only when the token after the `(` proves it cannot, without entering the

004629: // a type, qualifier, tag, typeof or _Atomic keyword, a decoration
004630: // c_ir_primitive_type_kind steps over (an attribute, an asm label, a `[[`
004631: // attribute) or an identifier naming a typedef, and nothing else, so:
004632: // - a number, a string, a character and every punctuator but `[` is refused

004635: //   enumerator or function is refused too: the prefix reads that binding

006521: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_memory_load(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CIntegerIrLocal* local, CToken token)
006522: {
006523:     IrType* place_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, local->type);
006524:     bool atomic = place_type && place_type->is_atomic;
006525:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
006526:     if (atomic && !builder->preparing_calls && c_ir_wide_atomic_runtime_required(builder, local->type))
006527:     {
006528:         result = c_ir_emit_wide_atomic_runtime_load(builder, local->place, local->type, c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token),
006529:                                                     IR_MEMORY_ORDER_SEQUENTIAL);
006530:     }
006531:     else
006532:     {
006533:         // The named-local load reads a qualified place at its unqualified type the
006534:         // same way c_ir_emit_load_place_raw does; the two must agree or the same
006535:         // object read through the two paths produces two different value types.
006536:         IrTypeId result_type = place_type && (atomic || place_type->is_volatile) ? place_type->unqualified_type : local->type;
006537:         result = c_ir_add_result(builder, result_type);
006538:         if (local->place.value < builder->function->value_count)
006539:         {
006540:             c_ir_label_metadata_copy_for_place(builder, local->place);
006541:             builder->function->values[result.value].points_to_read_only = builder->function->values[local->place.value].points_to_read_only;
006542:             if (builder->label_metadata_enabled)
006543:             {
006544:                 ir_label_provenance_load(builder->arena, builder->function, result, local->place);
006545:             }
006546:         }
006547:         IrValueId* operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
006548:         operands[0] = local->place;
006549:         IrSourceRange instruction_source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
006550:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(atomic ? IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_LOAD : IR_OPCODE_LOAD, result_type);
006551:         instruction.operands = operands;
006552:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
006553:         instruction.canonical_local = local->id;
006554:         instruction.result = result;
006555:         instruction.memory_order = atomic ? IR_MEMORY_ORDER_SEQUENTIAL : IR_MEMORY_ORDER_COUNT;
006556:         instruction.volatile_access = local->place.value < builder->function->value_count && builder->function->values[local->place.value].is_volatile;
006557:         IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, instruction_source);
006558:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
006559:     }
006560:     return result;
006561: }

006567:                              : c_ir_emit_memory_load(builder, local, token);
006568:     c_ir_vla_loaded_shape(builder, result, local->place);

006600: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_binary_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId left, IrValueId right, IrTypeId type, IrBinaryOperation operation,
006601:                                                      IrSourceRange source)
006602: {
006603:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
006604:     IrTypeId left_type = left.value < builder->function->value_count ? builder->function->values[left.value].canonical_type : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
006605:     IrTypeId right_type = right.value < builder->function->value_count ? builder->function->values[right.value].canonical_type : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
006606:     bool binary16_operands = c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, left_type) && c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, right_type);
006607:     bool arithmetic = operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY ||
006608:                       operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_DIVIDE;
006609:     bool comparison = operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_EQUAL || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_NOT_EQUAL || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_LESS ||
006610:                       operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_LESS_EQUAL || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_GREATER || operation == IR_BINARY_FLOAT_GREATER_EQUAL;
006611:     if (binary16_operands && (arithmetic || comparison))
006612:     {
006613:         IrValueId left_wide = c_ir_emit_float16_runtime_call(builder, S8("__extendhfsf2"), builder->f32_type, left, left_type, source);
006614:         IrValueId right_wide = c_ir_emit_float16_runtime_call(builder, S8("__extendhfsf2"), builder->f32_type, right, right_type, source);
006615:         if (left_wide.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && right_wide.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
006616:         {
006617:             IrValueId wide_result = c_ir_emit_binary_value_raw(builder, left_wide, right_wide, comparison ? type : builder->f32_type, operation, source);
006618:             if (comparison)
006619:             {
006620:                 result = wide_result;
006621:             }
006622:             else if (wide_result.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
006623:             {
006624:                 result = c_ir_emit_float16_runtime_call(builder, S8("__truncsfhf2"), type, wide_result, builder->f32_type, source);
006625:             }
006626:         }
006627:     }
006628:     else
006629:     {
006630:         result = c_ir_emit_binary_value_raw(builder, left, right, type, operation, source);
006631:     }
006632:     return result;
006633: }

006757: // The address of the bytes a bit-field occupies, as `unsigned char*`.
006758: // `c_ir_emit_address_of_place` refuses a bit-field place because C does --
006759: // `&s.b` is not an expression -- but a field with no single storage unit is
006760: // read and written one piece at a time, and the pieces past the first are
006761: // bytes the member place cannot name. The place still starts at
006762: // `field->offset`, which is the first byte of the span.
006763: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_bit_field_storage_address(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrSourceRange source)
006764: {
006765:     IrTypeId place_type = builder->function->values[place.value].canonical_type;
006766:     IrTypeId pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, place_type);
006767:     IrTypeId byte_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR));
006768:     if (pointer_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || byte_pointer_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
006769:     {
006770:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
006771:     }
006772:     IrValueId address = c_ir_add_result(builder, pointer_type);
006773:     if (address.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
006774:     {
006775:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
006776:     }
006777:     builder->function->values[address.value].points_to_read_only = builder->function->values[place.value].is_read_only;
006778:     IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_ADDRESS_OF, pointer_type);
006779:     instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
006780:     instruction.operands[0] = place;
006781:     instruction.operand_count = 1;
006782:     instruction.result = address;
006783:     IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
006784:     builder->function->values[address.value].definition = id;
006785:     return c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, byte_pointer_type, source);
006786: }

006807: // The bits of `field` that lie in one piece of its span, as the half-open
006808: // range [`low`, `high`) of span bit positions. Empty when the piece holds none

006812: {

006817:     *high = BUSTER_MIN(piece_high, field_high);

006820: // A packed bit-field the aggregate left no single storage unit for is read one
006821: // piece at a time and reassembled: each piece contributes the bits of its own
006822: // byte range that belong to the field, shifted down to the field's low bit.

007090: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_place_may_have_static_storage(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place)
007091: {
007092:     u32 value = place.value;
007093:     u32 steps = builder->function->value_count + 1;
007094:     while (value < builder->function->value_count && steps)
007095:     {
007096:         steps -= 1;
007097:         IrValue* current = builder->function->values + value;
007098:         IrInstructionId definition = current->definition;
007099:         if (definition.value >= builder->function->instruction_count)
007100:         {
007101:             return true;
007102:         }
007103:         IrInstruction* instruction = builder->function->instructions + definition.value;
007104:         if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_GLOBAL)
007105:         {
007106:             return true;
007107:         }
007108:         if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_LOCAL)
007109:         {
007110:             return false;
007111:         }
007112:         if ((instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_FIELD || instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_INDEX || instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_DEREFERENCE ||
007113:              instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_ADDRESS_OF || instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_CAST) &&
007114:             instruction->operand_count >= 1 && instruction->operands)
007115:         {
007116:             value = instruction->operands[0].value;
007117:             continue;
007118:         }
007119:         return true;
007120:     }
007121:     return true;
007122: }

007788: // Do two types agree closely enough that a function prototype built from them
007789: // is the same prototype? Identical ids always do. Beyond that only the coarse
007790: // shape is compared -- the kind, and for the scalar kinds the width and
007791: // signedness -- because two spellings of one aggregate can reach here as two
007792: // ids and refusing them would reject valid code. This is the deliberate
007793: // conservatism c_ir_function_prototypes_compatible documents.
007794: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_scalar_shapes_agree(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId left, IrTypeId right)
007795: {
007796:     IrType* left_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, left);
007797:     IrType* right_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, right);
007798:     bool result = left.value == right.value;
007799:     if (!result && left_type && right_type && left_type->kind == right_type->kind)
007800:     {
007801:         result = left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER && left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT && left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN;
007802:         result = result || (left_type->bit_width == right_type->bit_width && left_type->is_signed == right_type->is_signed &&
007803:                             (left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT || left_type->float_format == right_type->float_format));
007804:     }
007805: 
007806:     return result;
007807: }

007996: // Whether a promoted-member search has already queued `type`.
007997: //
007998: // The two searches below (this one and c_ir_promoted_member_path) walk the
007999: // anonymous nested aggregates of one struct or union, so their work lists hold
008000: // a handful of entries and almost always exactly one. Both used to answer this
008001: // question with a `bool` array indexed by type id, allocated and memset per
008002: // call over the whole program type table: 72.167 calls at a mean capacity of
008003: // 17.432 types, 1,26 GB of zeroing per self-host compile, 6,74% of every
008004: // stage-1 L1d miss for a set that never held more than a few members (audit
008005: // 2026-08-22T084855Z). The work list is the visited set; scanning it costs
008006: // less than clearing the table did.
008007: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_type_queued(const IrTypeId* queued, u32 count, IrTypeId type)
008008: {
008009:     bool found = false;
008010:     for (u32 index = 0; index < count; index += 1)
008011:     {
008012:         if (queued[index].value == type.value)
008013:         {
008014:             found = true;
008015:             break;
008016:         }
008017:     }
008018:     return found;
008019: }

008381: {

008403:         }

008408:         // stale metadata.

008935: // The imaginary suffix of a floating literal. C's suffixes are `f`/`l` and
008936: // GNU adds `i`/`j` for an imaginary constant, in either order and either
008937: // case, so the run of trailing letters is scanned rather than just the last
008938: // one. Reports the spelling with the imaginary letter removed, which is an
008939: // ordinary real literal the parser below already understands; `arena` is only
008940: // touched when that letter is not the last one.
008941: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_number_imaginary_spelling(Arena* arena, String8 spelling, String8* real_out)
008942: {
008943:     u64 suffix_start = spelling.length;
008944:     u64 imaginary_index = spelling.length;
008945:     while (suffix_start)
008946:     {
008947:         u8 byte = (u8)spelling.pointer[suffix_start - 1];
008948:         if (byte == 'i' || byte == 'I' || byte == 'j' || byte == 'J')
008949:         {
008950:             // Two imaginary letters is not a literal any compiler accepts;
008951:             // leave it alone and let the real parser refuse the spelling.
008952:             if (imaginary_index != spelling.length)
008953:             {
008954:                 return false;
008955:             }
008956:             imaginary_index = suffix_start - 1;
008957:         }
008958:         else if (byte != 'f' && byte != 'F' && byte != 'l' && byte != 'L')
008959:         {
008960:             break;
008961:         }
008962:         suffix_start -= 1;
008963:     }
008964:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length || !suffix_start)
008965:     {
008966:         return false;
008967:     }
008968:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length - 1)
008969:     {
008970:         *real_out = (String8){.pointer = spelling.pointer, .length = spelling.length - 1};
008971:         return true;
008972:     }
008973:     char8* copy = arena_allocate(arena, char8, spelling.length - 1);
008974:     memcpy(copy, spelling.pointer, imaginary_index);
008975:     memcpy(copy + imaginary_index, spelling.pointer + imaginary_index + 1, spelling.length - imaginary_index - 1);
008976:     *real_out = (String8){.pointer = copy, .length = spelling.length - 1};
008977:     return true;
008978: }
008979: 
008980: // The suffix of a floating constant: how many trailing bytes it occupies and
008981: // which type it names, reported as one code. C's suffixes are `f`/`F` for
008982: // float and `l`/`L` for long double, and C23 adds `f16`/`F16` for `_Float16`
008983: // -- the only one longer than a letter, so reading the last byte alone cannot
008984: // recognize it. The half suffix reports as 'h', a letter C does not use as a
008985: // suffix, so a caller comparing against 'f' or 'l' cannot confuse the two.
008986: // Every spelling-to-value path shares this so that the type a literal is
008987: // given and the digits that are parsed for it cannot disagree.
008988: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u32 c_ir_float_suffix(String8 spelling, char8* code_out)
008989: {
008990:     // In a hexadecimal spelling `f` and `F` are digits, and only a `p`
008991:     // exponent makes such a spelling a floating constant at all: `0x2f16` is
008992:     // the integer 12054 and `0x2f` the integer 47, where `0x1p4f` really does
008993:     // carry the float suffix. Asking for the exponent is what keeps a
008994:     // float-typed initializer written with a hexadecimal integer from losing
008995:     // its last digits to a suffix that is not there.
008996:     bool hexadecimal = spelling.length >= 2 && spelling.pointer[0] == '0' && (spelling.pointer[1] == 'x' || spelling.pointer[1] == 'X');
008997:     bool suffixable = !hexadecimal;
008998:     for (u64 index = 2; !suffixable && index < spelling.length; index += 1)
@@ src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:12318-12432 (match 12363) @@

015672: // Which arithmetic each operator gets is Clang's, checked against
015673: // `clang -O0 -S -emit-llvm` for every combination rather than derived:
015674: //   * `+` and `-` are componentwise, and a real operand touches only the real
015675: //     half (the imaginary half of the promoted real operand is a positive
015676: //     zero, and Clang carries the other operand's imaginary part through
015677: //     unchanged rather than adding it).
015678: //   * `*` and `/` with a real operand scale or divide both halves.
015679: //   * `*` and `/` with two complex operands call the compiler runtime --
015680: //     __mulsc3/__muldc3/__multc3 and __divsc3/__divdc3/__divtc3 -- which is
015681: //     what Clang emits without -ffast-math or -fcx-limited-range. Those
015682: //     helpers implement the overflow- and NaN-recovering forms from C11
015683: //     Annex G, and calling them rather than inlining Smith's algorithm is the
015684: //     choice made here: it is bit-for-bit what a Clang-built object does, and
015685: //     the alternative would be a second, subtly different implementation of
015686: //     the same numerics living in this file.
015687: //   * `real / complex` also goes to the runtime, with the numerator's
015688: //     imaginary part passed as a positive zero, again matching Clang.
015689: //   * `==` and `!=` compare both halves.
015690: //
015691: // System V x86-64 returns a `long double _Complex` in ST(0)/ST(1) (the psABI's
015692: // COMPLEX_X87 class) where the equivalent struct is returned in memory. That
015693: // is the one place the aggregate model is not the ABI, and it is the only
015694: // thing the backends had to learn about complex: the classifier gives that
015695: // result four X87/X87_UP eightbyte parts, the canonical x86-64 emitter pushes
015696: // the imaginary half and then the real one before its RET and pops them in
015697: // that order after a call, and every other position -- the argument, the
015698: // loads, the stores, the copies -- is the two-field aggregate unchanged.
015699:

015776:         return true;

016240:         }
016241:         return type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT ? c_ir_complex_zero(builder, type_id, source)
016242:                                            : c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, type_id);
016243:     }
016244:     IrTypeId element = complex_type->element_type;
016245:     IrValueId place = c_ir_complex_operand_place(builder, value, source);
016246:     if (place.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016247:     {
016248:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016249:     }
016250:     return c_ir_complex_part(builder, place, element, imaginary ? 1u : 0u, source);
016251: }

016253: // `+ - * /`, unary `-`, GNU unary `~` (conjugation) and `== !=` where at
016254: // least one operand is complex. Everything else -- the remaining bitwise and
016255: // the relational operators, `%` -- has no complex form in C and is refused
016256: // here rather than silently applied to the real half.
016257: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_apply_complex_operation(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CConditionalOperator operation, IrValueId* values, u32* value_count,
016258:                                                       u32 first, u32 operand_count, IrSourceRange source)
016259: {
016260:     IrTypeId left_type = builder->function->values[values[first].value].canonical_type;
016261:     IrTypeId right_type = operand_count == 2 ? builder->function->values[values[first + 1].value].canonical_type : left_type;
016262:     IrTypeId result_type = c_ir_complex_result_type(builder, left_type, right_type);
016263:     IrType* result_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, result_type);
016264:     if (!result_complex)
016265:     {
016266:         builder->failure_message = S8("unsupported complex operand type");
016267:         return false;
016268:     }
016269:     IrTypeId element = result_complex->element_type;
016270:     bool left_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, left_type) != 0;
016271:     bool right_complex = operand_count == 2 && c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, right_type) != 0;
016272:     IrValueId real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016273:     IrValueId imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016274:     if (operand_count == 1)
016275:     {
016276:         // GNU spells complex conjugation `~` -- C99 Annex G's `conj` -- so the
016277:         // one bitwise operator that has no complex form on a real operand does
016278:         // have one here. It negates the imaginary half alone; unary `-`
016279:         // negates both.
016280:         if (operation != C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS && operation != C_CONDITIONAL_BITWISE_NOT)
016281:         {
016282:             builder->failure_message = S8("this unary operator has no complex form");
016283:             return false;
016284:         }
016285:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016286:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &real, &imaginary, source))
016287:         {
016288:             return false;
016289:         }
016290:         real = operation == C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS ? c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, real, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source) : real;
016291:         imaginary = c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, imaginary, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source);
016292:         IrValueId negated = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016293:         if (negated.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016294:         {
016295:             return false;
016296:         }
016297:         *value_count = first;
016298:         values[(*value_count)++] = negated;
016299:         return true;
016300:     }
016301:     // Both operands are read before anything is emitted for the operation, so
016302:     // the two splits below cannot interleave with each other's field loads.
016303:     IrValueId left_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016304:     IrValueId left_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016305:     IrValueId right_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016306:     IrValueId right_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016307:     if (left_complex)
016308:     {
016309:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016310:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &left_real, &left_imaginary, source))
016311:         {
@@ src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:18200-18314 (match 18245) @@
018200:                 .call_index = child,
018201:             };
018202:         }
018203:     }
018204:     BUSTER_CHECK(emission_count == remaining);
018205:     *emission_order_out = emission_order;
018206:     *emission_count_out = emission_count;
018207:     return true;
018208: }

018210: // The one vector type the 512-bit vocabulary speaks in: 64 bytes of u8. Every
018211: // builtin that returns a vector returns this, and `Simd512` in
018212: // <buster/lib/simd.h> is declared to match, so no conversion ever appears at a
018213: // call site. The layout matches what the `vector_size` attribute produces for
018214: // the same spelling, so the two are the same IR type and not two that happen to
018215: // agree.
018216: // __builtin_popcount is one instruction where the target has POPCNT and the
018217: // classic SWAR sequence where it does not, decided here rather than in the
018218: // backends: an IR expansion is the same handful of ordinary instructions every
018219: // backend already emits, and it keeps AArch64 from needing a NEON round trip
018220: // for a scalar operation the compiler itself barely uses.
018221: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_population_count(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, CToken token, IrSourceRange source)
018222: {
018223:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
018224:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
018225:     {
018226:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018227:     }
018228:     if (target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_POPCNT))
018229:     {
018230:         IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
018231:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
018232:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
018233:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
018234:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
018235:         instruction.unary_operation = IR_UNARY_INTEGER_POPULATION_COUNT;
018236:         instruction.result = result;
018237:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
018238:         return result;
018239:     }
018240:     // The classic SWAR sequence: subtract the odd bits to make two-bit sums,
018241:     // add the pairs into four-bit sums, fold to bytes, then let one multiply
018242:     // gather every byte sum into the top byte.
018243:     u32 width = integer->bit_width;
018244:     u64 mask = width >= 64 ? UINT64_MAX : (((u64)1 << width) - 1);
018245:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 1, false, token, type);
018246:     IrValueId odd_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x5555555555555555) & mask, false, token, type);
018247:     IrValueId shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, one, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018248:     IrValueId high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, odd_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018249:     IrValueId value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_SUBTRACT, source);
018250:     IrValueId two = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 2, false, token, type);
018251:     IrValueId pair_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x3333333333333333) & mask, false, token, type);
018252:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, two, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018253:     high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018254:     IrValueId low = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018255:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, low, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018256:     IrValueId four = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, token, type);
018257:     IrValueId nibble_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f) & mask, false, token, type);
018258:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, four, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018259:     IrValueId summed = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, shifted, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018260:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, summed, nibble_mask, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018261:     IrValueId ones = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0101010101010101) & mask, false, token, type);
018262:     IrValueId gathered = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, ones, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_MULTIPLY, source);
018263:     IrValueId top = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width - 8, false, token, type);
018264:     return c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, gathered, top, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018265: }

018267: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_simd_vector_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder)
018268: {
018269:     IrTypeId element = builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR];
018270:     IrType* element_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, element);
018271:     if (!element_type || element_type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER || element_type->bit_width != 8)
018272:     {
018273:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
018274:     }
018275:     for (u32 type_index = 0; type_index < builder->program->types.count; type_index += 1)
018276:     {
018277:         IrType* candidate = builder->program->types.types + type_index;
018278:         if (candidate->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR && candidate->element_type.value == element.value && candidate->element_count == 64 &&
018279:             candidate->layout.size == 64)
018280:         {
018281:             return candidate->id;
018282:         }
018283:     }
018284:     return ir_program_add_type(builder->program, (IrType){
018285:                                                      .name = S8("GNU vector"),
018286:                                                      .element_type = element,
018287:                                                      .return_type = IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
018288:                                                      .layout =
018289:                                                          {
018290:                                                              .size = 64,
018291:                                                              .alignment = 64,
018292:                                                              .resolved = true,
018293:                                                          },
018294:                                                      .kind = IR_TYPE_VECTOR,
018295:                                                      .element_count = 64,
018296:                                                      .bit_width = 512,
018297:                                                  });
018298: }

018307:                  c_ir_simd_vector_type(builder);

018210: // The one vector type the 512-bit vocabulary speaks in: 64 bytes of u8. Every
018211: // builtin that returns a vector returns this, and `Simd512` in
018212: // <buster/lib/simd.h> is declared to match, so no conversion ever appears at a
018213: // call site. The layout matches what the `vector_size` attribute produces for
018214: // the same spelling, so the two are the same IR type and not two that happen to
018215: // agree.
018216: // __builtin_popcount is one instruction where the target has POPCNT and the
018217: // classic SWAR sequence where it does not, decided here rather than in the
018218: // backends: an IR expansion is the same handful of ordinary instructions every
018219: // backend already emits, and it keeps AArch64 from needing a NEON round trip
018220: // for a scalar operation the compiler itself barely uses.
018221: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_population_count(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, CToken token, IrSourceRange source)
018222: {
018223:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
018224:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
018225:     {
018226:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018227:     }
018228:     if (target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_POPCNT))
018229:     {
018230:         IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
018231:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
018232:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
018233:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
018234:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
018235:         instruction.unary_operation = IR_UNARY_INTEGER_POPULATION_COUNT;
018236:         instruction.result = result;
018237:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
018238:         return result;
018239:     }
018240:     // The classic SWAR sequence: subtract the odd bits to make two-bit sums,
018241:     // add the pairs into four-bit sums, fold to bytes, then let one multiply
018242:     // gather every byte sum into the top byte.
018243:     u32 width = integer->bit_width;
018244:     u64 mask = width >= 64 ? UINT64_MAX : (((u64)1 << width) - 1);
018245:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 1, false, token, type);
018246:     IrValueId odd_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x5555555555555555) & mask, false, token, type);
018247:     IrValueId shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, one, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018248:     IrValueId high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, odd_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018249:     IrValueId value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_SUBTRACT, source);
018250:     IrValueId two = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 2, false, token, type);
018251:     IrValueId pair_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x3333333333333333) & mask, false, token, type);
018252:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, two, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018253:     high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018254:     IrValueId low = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018255:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, low, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018256:     IrValueId four = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, token, type);
018257:     IrValueId nibble_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f) & mask, false, token, type);
018258:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, four, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018259:     IrValueId summed = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, shifted, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018260:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, summed, nibble_mask, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018261:     IrValueId ones = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0101010101010101) & mask, false, token, type);
018262:     IrValueId gathered = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, ones, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_MULTIPLY, source);
018263:     IrValueId top = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width - 8, false, token, type);
018264:     return c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, gathered, top, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018265: }

018221: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_population_count(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, CToken token, IrSourceRange source)
018222: {
018223:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
018224:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
018225:     {
018226:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018227:     }
018228:     if (target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_POPCNT))
018229:     {
018230:         IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);

018232:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
018233:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
018234:         instruction.operand_count = 1;

018237:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
018238:         return result;

018248:     IrValueId high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, odd_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018249:     IrValueId value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_SUBTRACT, source);
018250:     IrValueId two = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 2, false, token, type);
018251:     IrValueId pair_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x3333333333333333) & mask, false, token, type);
018252:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, two, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018253:     high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018254:     IrValueId low = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018255:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, low, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018256:     IrValueId four = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, token, type);
018257:     IrValueId nibble_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f) & mask, false, token, type);
018258:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, four, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);

018425: // Aggregate exchanges compare the promoted object's representation. Keep the
018426: // atomic instruction integer-typed: two pointer views name the same object,
018427: // and private scalar storage carries values between the record and its bits.
018428: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_place(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId object_type,
018429:                                                             IrTypeId bits_type, IrSourceRange source)
018430: {
018431:     IrType* object = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, object_type);
018432:     IrType* bits = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, bits_type);
018433:     // GNU's generic forms name an ordinary object, while C11 aggregate
018434:     // exchange/CAS name an atomic-qualified one. In both cases the integer
018435:     // view must cover exactly the storage the caller supplied.
018436:     bool valid = object && bits && object->layout.resolved && bits->layout.resolved &&
018437:                  object->layout.size == bits->layout.size && bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
018438:     IrTypeId atomic_bits = valid ? c_ir_add_qualified_type(builder->program, bits_type, true, object->is_volatile) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
018439:     IrTypeId pointer_type = valid ? c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, atomic_bits) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
018440:     IrValueId address = valid ? c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, place, object_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018441:     IrValueId cast = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018442:     IrValueId result = cast.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, cast, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018443:     return result;
018444: }

018446: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId record_type,
018447:                                                             IrTypeId bits_type, bool to_bits, IrSourceRange source)
018448: {
018449:     IrType* record = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, record_type);
018450:     IrType* bits = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, bits_type);
018451:     bool valid = record && bits && record->layout.resolved && bits->layout.resolved && record->layout.size <= bits->layout.size &&
018452:                  value.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
018453:     IrValueId slot = valid ? c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018454:     IrTypeId pointer_type = valid ? c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, record_type) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
018455:     IrValueId address = valid ? c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018456:     IrValueId cast = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018457:     IrValueId record_place = cast.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, cast, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018458:     valid = valid && record_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
018459:     if (valid && to_bits)
018460:     {
018461:         // A three-byte record uses a four-byte atomic object. Initialize the
018462:         // promoted tail before writing the record, matching aggregate stores.
018463:         IrValueId zero = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
018464:         valid = zero.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, bits_type, zero, source) &&
018465:                 c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, record_place, record_type, value, source);
018466:     }
018467:     else if (valid)
018468:     {
018469:         valid = c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, bits_type, value, source);
018470:     }
018471:     IrValueId result = valid ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, to_bits ? slot : record_place, to_bits ? bits_type : record_type, source)
018472:                             : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018473:     return result;
018474: }

022834: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_emit_compound_assignment(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId type, CConditionalOperator operation,
022835:                                                        IrValueId right, IrSourceRange source, IrValueId* previous_out, IrValueId* result_out)
022836: {
022837:     IrType* place_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
022838:     bool atomic = place_type && place_type->is_atomic;
022839:     // The operation consumes an unqualified value even when the destination
022840:     // place is volatile. Loads and stores retain that place's access flags.
022841:     IrTypeId value_type = place_type && (atomic || place_type->is_volatile) ? place_type->unqualified_type : type;
022842:     IrType* unqualified = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, value_type);
022843:     bool pointer_arithmetic = unqualified && unqualified->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER && (operation == C_CONDITIONAL_ADD || operation == C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT);
022844:     IrValueId previous = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
022845:     IrValueId operation_right = right;
022846:     if (pointer_arithmetic && atomic)
022847:     {
022848:         IrType* element = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, unqualified->element_type);
022849:         right = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, right, builder->ptrdiff_type, source);
022850:         if (!element || !element->layout.resolved || !element->layout.size || right.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
022851:         {
022852:             return false;
022853:         }
022854:         IrValueId scale = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, element->layout.size, false, (CToken){0}, builder->ptrdiff_type);
022855:         right = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, right, scale, builder->ptrdiff_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_MULTIPLY, source);
022856:     }
022857:     else if (!pointer_arithmetic && !c_ir_unsigned_bit_field_promotes_to_int(builder, c_ir_bit_field_from_place(builder, place)))

022860:         operation_right = right;
022861:     }

022864:         return false;
022865:     }

022867:     {

022869:         // one is a compare-exchange loop over the object's bit pattern rather
022870:         // than a single instruction.
022871:         return c_ir_emit_atomic_float_update(builder, place, type, value_type, operation, operation_right, source, previous_out, result_out);
022872:     }

022875:         IrAtomicOperation atomic_operation = IR_ATOMIC_OPERATION_COUNT;
022876:         if (!unqualified || (unqualified->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER && !pointer_arithmetic) || !c_ir_atomic_operation(operation, &atomic_operation))
022877:         {
022878:             return false;
022879:         }
022880:         previous = c_ir_add_result(builder, value_type);
022881:         IrValueId* operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 2);
022882:         operands[0] = place;
022883:         operands[1] = right;
022884:         IrSourceRange instruction_source = source;
022885:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_READ_MODIFY_WRITE, value_type);
022886:         instruction.operands = operands;

022888:         instruction.memory_order = IR_MEMORY_ORDER_SEQUENTIAL;
022889:         instruction.atomic_operation = (u8)atomic_operation;

022891:         IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, instruction_source);
022892:         builder->function->values[previous.value].definition = id;
022893:     }
022894:     else
022895:     {
022896:         previous = c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, place, type, source);
022897:     }
022898:     IrValueId values[2] = {
022899:         previous,
022900:         operation_right,
022901:     };

022903:     if (previous.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_apply_operation(builder, operation, values, &value_count, source, value_type) || value_count != 1 ||
022904:         (!atomic && !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, place, type, values[0], source)))
022905:     {

023840: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_increment(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId type, IrValueId previous, CToken token, bool prefix)
023841: {
023842:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value(builder, 1, false, token);
023843:     IrType* place_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
023844:     if (place_type && place_type->is_atomic)
023845:     {

023847:         IrValueId atomic_result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;

023849:                                            c_token_is_punctuator(&token, C_PUNCTUATOR_PLUS_PLUS) ? C_CONDITIONAL_ADD : C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT, one,
023850:                                            c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token), &atomic_previous, &atomic_result))
023851:         {
023852:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
023853:         }
023854:         return prefix ? atomic_result : atomic_previous;
023855:     }

023857:         previous,
023858:         one,
023859:     };

023861:     IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
023862:     if (!c_ir_apply_operation(builder, c_token_is_punctuator(&token, C_PUNCTUATOR_PLUS_PLUS) ? C_CONDITIONAL_ADD : C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT, values, &value_count,

023865:     {
023866:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
023867:     }
023868:     if (prefix && values[0].value < builder->function->value_count && builder->function->values[values[0].value].canonical_type.value != type.value)
023869:     {
023870:         // `++E` has the value E holds after the store, which is the value in
023871:         // E's own type: the addition ran in the promoted type, so a narrower
023872:         // object's result has to come back down before anything reads it.
023873:         // SQLite carries its page-header cell count into the high byte with
023874:         // `if( (++data[hdr+4])==0 ) data[hdr+3]++;`, and that carry is lost

023879: }

023990: // Large aggregate zero initialization must not expand into one canonical
023991: // value and spill slot per byte. Windows ARM64 unwind records cannot describe
023992: // the multi-megabyte functions that expansion produces. Check representations
023993: // and qualifiers before using a byte loop; this introduces no libc dependency.

024002:     IrValueId cursor = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, builder->size_type, source);
024003:     IrValueId initial = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, token, builder->size_type);

024006:     IrValueId zero = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, token, element_type);

028430:     // c_ir_emit_nullptr gives: it saves the widening cast on the hottest
028431:     // conversion in the language.
028432:     IrTypeId zero_type = type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER ? builder->size_type : builder->s32_type;
028433:     IrValueId zero = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, zero_type);
028434:     if (zero.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && type_id.value != zero_type.value)
028435:     {
028436:         IrType* integer_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, builder->s32_type);
028437:         IrConversionOperation conversion = IR_CONVERSION_COUNT;
028438:         if (integer_type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
028439:         {
028440:             conversion = integer_type->bit_width < type->bit_width
028441:                              ? (integer_type->is_signed ? IR_CONVERSION_INTEGER_SIGN_EXTEND : IR_CONVERSION_INTEGER_ZERO_EXTEND)
028442:                          : integer_type->bit_width > type->bit_width ? IR_CONVERSION_INTEGER_TRUNCATE
028443:                                                                     : IR_CONVERSION_INTEGER_REINTERPRET;
028444:         }
028445:         else if (type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT)
028446:         {
028447:             conversion = IR_CONVERSION_SIGNED_INTEGER_TO_FLOAT;
028448:         }
028449:         if (type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER)
028450:         {
028451:             zero = c_ir_emit_integer_to_pointer(builder, zero, type_id, source);
028452:         }
028453:         else
028454:         {
028455:             zero = conversion == IR_CONVERSION_COUNT ? IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID
028456:                                                      : c_ir_emit_cast_instruction(builder, zero, type_id, conversion, source);
028457:         }
028458:     }
028459:     if (zero.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
028460:     {
028461:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
028462:     }
028463:     IrBinaryOperation operation = type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER   ? IR_BINARY_INTEGER_NOT_EQUAL
028464:                                   : type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT   ? IR_BINARY_FLOAT_NOT_EQUAL
028465:                                   : type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER ? IR_BINARY_POINTER_NOT_EQUAL
028466:                                                                   : IR_BINARY_COUNT;
028467:     if (operation == IR_BINARY_COUNT)
028468:     {
028469:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
028470:     }
028471:     IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, builder->bool_type);
028472:     IrValueId* operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 2);
028473:     operands[0] = value;
028474:     operands[1] = zero;
028475:     IrSourceRange comparison_source = source;
028476:     IrInstruction comparison = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_BINARY, builder->bool_type);
028477:     comparison.operands = operands;
028478:     comparison.operand_count = 2;
028479:     comparison.binary_operation = (u8)operation;
028480:     comparison.result = result;
028481:     IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, comparison, comparison_source);
028482:     builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
028483:     return result;
028484: }

038477:     bool stepping = true;

038481:         if (!state->yielded)

038483:             c_ir_lower_frame_finish(builder, success, state->result);

038495:             // suspension resumes through the loop unchanged.

041737: // The scalar leaves of an aggregate initializer, classified before they are
041738: // folded.  Almost every leaf of a large table is one number -- the generated
041739: // instruction metadata is arrays of small integer records -- and the general
041740: // folder (c_ir_constant_initializer_bytes_legacy) prices each at a task
041741: // array, a compound-literal probe, a query frame, the shunting-yard
041742: // evaluator, a cast and a byte loop.  A leaf whose tokens are exactly a
041743: // number, a signed number, a character constant or an identifier naming an
041744: // integer constant, landing in an integer, boolean, enum or float member
041745: // that is not a bit-field, is folded here
041746: // instead: the same literal routines and typing rules the evaluator uses
041747: // (c_ir_integer_literal_type, c_ir_float_literal_value,
041748: // c_ir_decode_character_value), the evaluator's unary `+`/`-`
041749: // (c_ir_constant_apply_unary) and its cast (c_ir_constant_cast), then one
041750: // little-endian store of the member's size.  The class is one byte decided
041751: // from the token kinds and the member's kind alone; an arm that cannot
041752: // reproduce the evaluator's answer -- a literal no type holds, a 128-bit
041753: // operand, an imaginary suffix -- declines, and the leaf takes the general
041754: // folder, so every refusal and its message stay exactly what they were.
041755: // A big-endian target keeps the byte loop: only the little-endian store is
041756: // written here.
041757: typedef enum CIrInitializerLeafClass
041758: {
041759:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_OTHER,
041760:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_INTEGER_TO_INTEGER,
041761:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_INTEGER_TO_FLOAT,
041762:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_FLOAT_TO_FLOAT,
041763:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_CHARACTER_TO_INTEGER,
041764:     C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_IDENTIFIER_TO_INTEGER,
041765: } CIrInitializerLeafClass;
041766: 
041767: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_constant_identifier(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, u32 token_index, CIrConstantValue* result);
041768: 
041769: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u8 c_ir_constant_initializer_leaf_class(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrType* child, u32 start, u32 end)
041770: {
041771:     u8 leaf_class = C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_OTHER;
041772:     CToken* tokens = builder->preprocess.tokens;
041773:     u32 count = end - start;
041774:     bool signed_prefix =
041775:         count == 2 && (c_token_is_punctuator(&tokens[start], C_PUNCTUATOR_PLUS) || c_token_is_punctuator(&tokens[start], C_PUNCTUATOR_MINUS));
041776:     if ((count == 1 || signed_prefix) && builder->program->data_layout.endianness == TARGET_ENDIAN_LITTLE)
041777:     {
041778:         CToken literal = tokens[end - 1];
041779:         u64 size = child->layout.size;
041780:         // The sizes one u64 of bits fills: a wider member takes the general
041781:         // evaluator and the two-limb byte writer.
041782:         bool integer_child = (child->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || child->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || child->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM) &&
041783:                              (size == 1 || size == 2 || size == 4 || size == 8);
041784:         // binary16, f32 and f64: the x87 element has its own folder ahead of
041785:         // the general one, and any other width is stored through the general
041786:         // folder's own conversion.
041787:         bool float_child = child->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && ((child->bit_width == 16 && size == 2) || (child->bit_width == 32 && size == 4) ||
041788:                                                             (child->bit_width == 64 && size == 8));
041789:         if (literal.kind == C_TOKEN_PREPROCESSING_NUMBER)
041790:         {
041791:             bool floating = c_number_is_float(c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, literal));
041792:             if (integer_child && !floating)
041793:             {
041794:                 leaf_class = C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_INTEGER_TO_INTEGER;
041795:             }
041796:             else if (float_child)
041797:             {
041798:                 leaf_class = floating ? C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_FLOAT_TO_FLOAT : C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_INTEGER_TO_FLOAT;
041799:             }
041800:         }
041801:         else if (literal.kind == C_TOKEN_CHARACTER_LITERAL && integer_child)
041802:         {
041803:             leaf_class = C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_CHARACTER_TO_INTEGER;
041804:         }
041805:         else if (literal.kind == C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER && integer_child)
041806:         {
041807:             leaf_class = C_IR_INITIALIZER_LEAF_IDENTIFIER_TO_INTEGER;
041808:         }
041809:     }
041810:     return leaf_class;
041811: }

041813: // `size` bytes of `bits`, least significant first: what
041814: // c_ir_constant_store_unit_bits writes for a little-endian target and a
041815: // member no wider than the bits.  Spelled per size so the stores merge.
041816: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL void c_ir_constant_store_little_endian(u8* bytes, u64 size, u64 bits)
041817: {
041818:     switch (size)
041819:     {
041820:     case 1:
041821:         bytes[0] = (u8)bits;

041830:         bytes[2] = (u8)(bits >> 16);
041831:         bytes[3] = (u8)(bits >> 24);
041832:         break;
041833:     case 8:
041834:         bytes[0] = (u8)bits;
041835:         bytes[1] = (u8)(bits >> 8);
041836:         bytes[2] = (u8)(bits >> 16);

008959:         {

041737: // The scalar leaves of an aggregate initializer, classified before they are
041738: // folded.  Almost every leaf of a large table is one number -- the generated
041739: // instruction metadata is arrays of small integer records -- and the general
041740: // folder (c_ir_constant_initializer_bytes_legacy) prices each at a task
041741: // array, a compound-literal probe, a query frame, the shunting-yard
041742: // evaluator, a cast and a byte loop.  A leaf whose tokens are exactly a
041743: // number, a signed number, a character constant or an identifier naming an
041744: // integer constant, landing in an integer, boolean, enum or float member
041745: // that is not a bit-field, is folded here
041746: // instead: the same literal routines and typing rules the evaluator uses
041747: // (c_ir_integer_literal_type, c_ir_float_literal_value,
041748: // c_ir_decode_character_value), the evaluator's unary `+`/`-`
041749: // (c_ir_constant_apply_unary) and its cast (c_ir_constant_cast), then one
041750: // little-endian store of the member's size.  The class is one byte decided
041751: // from the token kinds and the member's kind alone; an arm that cannot
041752: // reproduce the evaluator's answer -- a literal no type holds, a 128-bit
041753: // operand, an imaginary suffix -- declines, and the leaf takes the general
041754: // folder, so every refusal and its message stay exactly what they were.
041755: // A big-endian target keeps the byte loop: only the little-endian store is
041756: // written here.

000001: // C -> canonical IR lowering, the third stage of the frontend. The entry
000002: // point is c_lower_to_ir at the bottom of the file: it sizes and fills one
000003: // IrProgram from the preprocessed token stream and the parser's entities,
000004: // scopes, and types, lowering every function body and global initializer.
000005: // There is no AST — lowering re-walks token ranges directly, resolving
000006: // identifiers through the parse result's scopes and answering structure
000007: // questions from a prebuilt matching-delimiter index
000008: // (c_ir_build_delimiter_index).
000009: // c_ir_parameter_value_type and c_ir_emit_parameter keep callable values
000010: // separate from the declared qualification of parameter objects.
000011: //
000012: // Source-dependent recursion is forbidden (AGENTS.md), so anything that
000013: // would recurse runs on an explicit machine owned by CIntegerIrBuilder:
000014: // - CIrVlaValue retains evaluated VLA extents and expression category until
000015: //   pointer consumers finish; c_ir_vla_* owns its sparse per-function table.
000016: // - CIrLowerMachine is the frame stack for statements and expressions.
000017: //   Each CIrLowerFrameKind pairs a *_step function (advance the frame one
000018: //   CIrLowerFrameStage) with a *_frame_push adapter, both dispatched by
000019: //   c_ir_lower_dispatch. c_ir_lower_body_advance walks statements through
000020: //   a CIrBodyTask list; c_ir_lower_expression_core_step evaluates
000021: //   expressions shunting-yard style over value and operator stacks. A new
000022: //   construct means a new frame kind, its step, its push adapter, and a
000023: //   dispatch case. A push site whose child kind is statically known may run
000024: //   the child's step directly and consume a completion in place (a
000025: //   suspension always resumes through the dispatch loop), and the
000026: //   BODY/BODY_ASSIGNMENT_STATEMENT steps self-loop over their own resumes;
000027: //   the direct-run edge set must stay acyclic — in particular the prepare
000028: //   steps and PREPARED_CALL never direct-run the EXPRESSION children they
000029: //   push, or expression nesting would recurse on the C stack.
000030: // - CIrQueryMachine answers compile-time questions the walk hits
000031: //   mid-expression — sizeof, type names, array bounds, offsetof, type
000032: //   prediction, null-pointer-constant tests (the c_ir_query_* entry
000033: //   points). A query that needs a sub-query suspends through CIrQueryResume
000034: //   and resumes past its finished prefix instead of re-evaluating it.
000035: //   A parenthesized group's type-name probe enters through
000036: //   c_ir_group_type_name (c_ir_query_group_type_name from inside the
000037: //   machine), which refuses a group whose first token proves it is no type
000038: //   name before the machine runs and memoizes the answer per opening
000039: //   parenthesis of the body.
000040: // - Calls are discovered and lowered before the surrounding expression
000041: //   consumes their values (c_ir_prepare_calls_discover,
000042: //   c_ir_emit_prepared_call_step), so the expression machine sees each
000043: //   call — builtins included — as one already-computed value. The exception
000044: //   is a call in an operand that runs only when a branch is taken — an arm of
000045: //   a conditional, the right side of && or ||, a _Generic association: that
000046: //   one is left unprepared, and whichever child expression owns the operand
000047: //   prepares it inside the block that actually runs.
000048: //
000049: // Layout, in file order; each anchor is a definition to search for:
000050: //   c_declaration_binding                         __attribute__((weak)) and
000051: //                                                 __attribute__((alias))
000052: //   c_ir_scalar_type .. c_ir_add_qualified_type   C type -> IrType mapping
000053: //                                                 and derived-type interning
000054: //   c_ir_function_signature                       signatures and ABI limits
000055: //   c_ir_emit_field_place_from_value              local/scratch member-search frontiers
000056: //   CIntegerIrBuilder                             per-module lowering state
000057: //   c_ir_label_metadata_*                         label provenance needed by
000058: //                                                 computed goto
000059: //   c_ir_ssa_*                                    sparse sealed-block local SSA
000060: //                                                 and memory-form fallback
000061: //   c_ir_emit_local .. c_ir_emit_parameter        place/value emission
000062: //                                                 primitives
000063: //   c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_*                  aggregate exchange/CAS
000064: //                                                 representation views
000065: //   c_ir_float_parse, c_ir_ieee_from_rational,    literals: exact rational ->
000066: //   c_ir_ext80_*, c_ir_decode_quoted,             IEEE/x87 conversion, string
000067: //   c_ir_count_quoted                             and character decoding
000068: //   c_ir_complex_compose, c_ir_complex_split    immutable complex construction
000069: //                                                 and scalar projection
000070: //   c_ir_emit_initializer_capture                exact constructor types and
000071: //                                                 qualified subobject stores
000072: //   c_ir_build_function_name_index                call-target resolution
000073: //   CIrLowerFrameKind .. c_ir_lower_dispatch      the lowering machines
000074: //   c_ir_lower_expression_core_step               the expression evaluator
000075: //   c_ir_cleanup_*                                __attribute__((cleanup))

016990: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL void c_ir_prepare_control_expressions_step(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CIrLowerFrame* frame)
016991: {
016992:     CIrLowerMachine* machine = &builder->lower_machine;
016993:     if (frame->stage == C_IR_LOWER_STAGE_BEGIN)
016994:     {
016995:         frame->as.prepare_control.index = frame->as.prepare_control.start;
016996:         frame->as.prepare_control.lazy = c_ir_lazy_operand_scan_start();
016997:         frame->stage = C_IR_LOWER_STAGE_FINISH;
016998:     }
016999:     else if (frame->stage == C_IR_LOWER_STAGE_CHILD)
017000:     {
017001:         if (!machine->child_result.success || frame->as.prepare_control.expression_index >= builder->prepared_control_expression_count)
017002:         {
017003:             c_ir_lower_frame_finish(builder, false, IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID);
017004:             return;
017005:         }
017006:         CIrPreparedControlExpression* expression =
017007:             builder->prepared_control_expressions + frame->as.prepare_control.expression_index;
017008:         expression->result = machine->child_result.value;
017009:         expression->lowering = false;
017010:         expression->emitted = true;
017011:         frame->as.prepare_control.index = frame->as.prepare_control.close + 1;
017012:         c_ir_lazy_operand_scan_skip_group(&frame->as.prepare_control.lazy);
017013:         frame->stage = C_IR_LOWER_STAGE_FINISH;
017014:     }
017015:     while (frame->as.prepare_control.index < frame->as.prepare_control.end)
017016:     {
017017:         u32 index = frame->as.prepare_control.index++;
017018:         c_ir_lazy_operand_scan_step(builder, &frame->as.prepare_control.lazy, frame->as.prepare_control.start,
017019:                                     frame->as.prepare_control.end, index);
017020:         if (index + 1 < frame->as.prepare_control.end &&
017021:             c_token_is_punctuator(&builder->preprocess.tokens[index + 1], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS) &&
017022:             c_ir_token_builtin_kind(builder, builder->preprocess.tokens[index]) == C_SYMBOL_BUILTIN_GENERIC)
017023:         {
017024:             u32 close = c_ir_matching_delimiter_cached(builder, index + 1, frame->as.prepare_control.end, C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS,
017025:                                                        C_PUNCTUATOR_RIGHT_PARENTHESIS);
017026:             if (close == UINT32_MAX)
017027:             {
017028:                 builder->failure_token_index = index;
017029:                 builder->failure_message = S8("unterminated _Generic selection");
017030:                 c_ir_lower_frame_finish(builder, false, IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID);
017031:                 return;
017032:             }
017033:             frame->as.prepare_control.index = close + 1;
017034:             continue;
017035:         }
017036:         bool parentheses = c_token_is_punctuator(&builder->preprocess.tokens[index], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS);
017037:         bool brackets = c_token_is_punctuator(&builder->preprocess.tokens[index], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_BRACKET);
017038:         // A token that opens no group leaves here. Every test below already
017039:         // stood inside a `parentheses || brackets` guard, and the group facts
017040:         // computed in between are pure, so this only moves the rejection ahead
017041:         // of the matching-delimiter query -- which for such a token asked for
017042:         // the close of a group its own token does not open, missed the stream
017043:         // index on the punctuator test, and answered with a linear scan of the
017044:         // whole remaining range. On a self-compile the loop steps over
017045:         // 1.659.024 tokens and 1.431.849 of those queries fell through to that
017046:         // scan.
017047:         if (!parentheses && !brackets)
017048:         {
017049:             continue;
017050:         }
017051:         CIrPreparedControlExpression* recorded = c_ir_prepared_control_expression_find(builder, index);
017052:         if (recorded)
017053:         {
017054:             // A group an earlier prepass already prepared has run its whole
017055:             // interior once. A nested prepass — the one a call-argument
017056:             // expression pushes over a range that contains the group — must
017057:             // jump past it, not step inside: rescanning the interior records
017058:             // an inner group a second time and runs its side effects again
017059:             // (tests/basic_c_conditional_operand.c, the nested-call shape).
