000001: // C -> canonical IR lowering, the third stage of the frontend. The entry
000002: // point is c_lower_to_ir at the bottom of the file: it sizes and fills one
000003: // IrProgram from the preprocessed token stream and the parser's entities,
000004: // scopes, and types, lowering every function body and global initializer.
000005: // There is no AST — lowering re-walks token ranges directly, resolving
000006: // identifiers through the parse result's scopes and answering structure
000007: // questions from a prebuilt matching-delimiter index
000008: // (c_ir_build_delimiter_index).
000009: // c_ir_parameter_value_type and c_ir_emit_parameter keep callable values
000010: // separate from the declared qualification of parameter objects.
000011: //
000012: // Source-dependent recursion is forbidden (AGENTS.md), so anything that
000013: // would recurse runs on an explicit machine owned by CIntegerIrBuilder:
000014: // - CIrVlaValue retains evaluated VLA extents and expression category until
000015: //   pointer consumers finish; c_ir_vla_* owns its sparse per-function table.
000016: // - CIrLowerMachine is the frame stack for statements and expressions.
000017: //   Each CIrLowerFrameKind pairs a *_step function (advance the frame one
000018: //   CIrLowerFrameStage) with a *_frame_push adapter, both dispatched by
000019: //   c_ir_lower_dispatch. c_ir_lower_body_advance walks statements through
000020: //   a CIrBodyTask list; c_ir_lower_expression_core_step evaluates
000021: //   expressions shunting-yard style over value and operator stacks. A new
000022: //   construct means a new frame kind, its step, its push adapter, and a
000023: //   dispatch case. A push site whose child kind is statically known may run
000024: //   the child's step directly and consume a completion in place (a
000025: //   suspension always resumes through the dispatch loop), and the
000026: //   BODY/BODY_ASSIGNMENT_STATEMENT steps self-loop over their own resumes;
000027: //   the direct-run edge set must stay acyclic — in particular the prepare
000028: //   steps and PREPARED_CALL never direct-run the EXPRESSION children they
000029: //   push, or expression nesting would recurse on the C stack.
000030: // - CIrQueryMachine answers compile-time questions the walk hits
000031: //   mid-expression — sizeof, type names, array bounds, offsetof, type
000032: //   prediction, null-pointer-constant tests (the c_ir_query_* entry
000033: //   points). A query that needs a sub-query suspends through CIrQueryResume
000034: //   and resumes past its finished prefix instead of re-evaluating it.
000035: //   A parenthesized group's type-name probe enters through
000036: //   c_ir_group_type_name (c_ir_query_group_type_name from inside the
000037: //   machine), which refuses a group whose first token proves it is no type
000038: //   name before the machine runs and memoizes the answer per opening
000039: //   parenthesis of the body.
000040: // - Calls are discovered and lowered before the surrounding expression
000041: //   consumes their values (c_ir_prepare_calls_discover,
000042: //   c_ir_emit_prepared_call_step), so the expression machine sees each
000043: //   call — builtins included — as one already-computed value. The exception
000044: //   is a call in an operand that runs only when a branch is taken — an arm of
000045: //   a conditional, the right side of && or ||, a _Generic association: that
000046: //   one is left unprepared, and whichever child expression owns the operand
000047: //   prepares it inside the block that actually runs.
000048: //

000106: // Which members of `interesting` — a union of C_SYMBOL_WELL_KNOWN_BIT values
000107: // — appear among a declaration's pre-body tokens, answered in one pass: an
000108: // interned identifier contributes a shift and a mask against the id the
000109: // token already carries, and only a token the intern pass never saw
000110: // (pasted, synthesized, or test-built) falls back to the spelling ladder,
000111: // so a missed path costs speed and never correctness. Every spelling the
000112: // callers ask about is identifier-shaped, so non-identifier tokens cannot
000113: // match and are skipped without materializing their spelling.
000114: // Every caller asks about declaration specifiers — storage class, `inline`,
000115: // thread locality — and those stand outside every delimiter, so a nested
000116: // token cannot answer this question and must not be counted. The depth is
000117: // what separates a specifier from an array parameter's `[static 3]`, where
000118: // `static` is a bound qualifier, and from a statement expression inside an
000119: // initializer, which carries declarations of its own.
000120: // `c_parse_local_declarations` tracks the same depth over the same range for
000121: // the same reason. An `__attribute__((...))` list is why the walk cannot
000122: // simply stop at the first delimiter instead: musl spells `hidden` as one,
000123: // ahead of the specifiers it must still find.
000124: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u64 c_declaration_well_known_set(CPreprocessResult preprocess, CDeclaration declaration, u64 interesting)
000125: {
000126:     u32 end = declaration.body_start ? declaration.body_start - 1 : declaration.token_start + declaration.token_count;
000127:     u64 result = 0;
000128:     u32 group_depth = 0;
000129:     for (u32 index = declaration.token_start; index < end; index += 1)
000130:     {
000131:         CToken token = preprocess.tokens[index];
000132:         if (token.kind != C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER)
000133:         {
000134:             group_depth += c_punctuator_in_set(token.punctuator, C_PUNCTUATOR_SET_DELIMITER_OPEN) ? 1 : 0;
000135:             group_depth -= group_depth && c_punctuator_in_set(token.punctuator, C_PUNCTUATOR_SET_DELIMITER_CLOSE) ? 1 : 0;
000136:         }
000137:         else if (!group_depth)
000138:         {
000139:             if (token.symbol)
000140:             {
000141:                 result |= token.symbol < 64 ? interesting & (1ull << token.symbol) : 0;
000142:             }
000143:             else
000144:             {
000145:                 String8 spelling = c_token_spelling(preprocess.spelling_base, token);
000146:                 for (u64 remaining = interesting; remaining; remaining &= remaining - 1)
000147:                 {
000148:                     if (string_equal(spelling, c_symbol_well_known_spellings[trailing_zeroes_u64(remaining)]))
000149:                     {
000150:                         result |= remaining & (0 - remaining);
000151:                     }
000152:                 }
000153:             }
000154:         }
000155:     }
000156: 
000157:     return result;
000158: }

004570: // The last local this token names, for the four sites whose token has no
004571: // resolved entity. A resolved global must never select a same-named local
004572: // from a scope that has ended.  All four ran a string_equal per
004573: // row: 24.940 fallbacks over 2,32 M rows on a self-compile, which is where the
004574: // lowering's 2,3 M memcmp calls came from, and string_equal is the worst
004575: // L1d-miss-per-cycle ratio of any ordinary symbol in the compile.  The intern
004576: // table is injective and both sides read the one spelling space, so two
004577: // nonzero symbols answer exactly what the two spellings answer; a row or token
004578: // the intern pass never saw still compares spellings, so a missed path costs
004579: // speed and never correctness.
004580: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL CIntegerIrLocal* c_ir_find_local_by_name(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token)
004581: {
004582:     CIntegerIrLocal* result = 0;
004583:     // Local rows and symbol rows are allocated together by c_lower_to_ir.
004584:     BUSTER_CHECK(!builder->local_count || (builder->locals && builder->local_symbols));
004585:     String8 spelling = c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, token);
004586:     for (u32 index = builder->local_count; index != 0 && !result; index -= 1)
004587:     {
004588:         u32 candidate_symbol = builder->local_symbols[index - 1];
004589:         bool same = token.symbol && candidate_symbol ? token.symbol == candidate_symbol : string_equal(builder->locals[index - 1].name, spelling);
004590:         if (same)
004591:         {
004592:             result = builder->locals + index - 1;
004593:         }
004594:     }
004595:     return result;
004596: }

004626: // May the parenthesized group opening at `open` spell a type name?  False
004627: // only when the token after the `(` proves it cannot, without entering the
004628: // query machine.  c_ir_type_name_prefix accepts a type name that begins with
004629: // a type, qualifier, tag, typeof or _Atomic keyword, a decoration
004630: // c_ir_primitive_type_kind steps over (an attribute, an asm label, a `[[`
004631: // attribute) or an identifier naming a typedef, and nothing else, so:
004632: // - a number, a string, a character and every punctuator but `[` is refused
004633: //   outright;
004634: // - an identifier the parser bound to a local, object, parameter,
004635: //   enumerator or function is refused too: the prefix reads that binding
004636: //   before any scope lookup, and none of them is a typedef.  Its spelling
004637: //   must not be one of the keywords above, which
004638: //   c_parse_type_name_start_word_token answers from the word bits (an
004639: //   interned spelling outside the predefined range is no keyword; symbol 0
004640: //   is unclassified and stays a candidate).

004642: // and a typedef is the candidate the probe exists for.
